subject: Critical Thinking
title: AI Ethics: Who's Responsible When the Algorithm Decides?
description: A quick win: understand AI Ethics: Who's Responsible When the Algorithm Decides?.

hook.text: A self-driving car must choose: hit the pedestrian or swerve & kill the passenger. Who programmed that choice?

buildup.text: AI systems make decisions about loans, parole, hiring, & medical diagnosis.

discovery.text: The 'responsibility gap': when decisions are made by algorithms, no single person chose the outcome. The programmer?

twist.text: Algorithms can produce bias even when no single engineer meant to discriminate.

climax.text: Ethical AI needs transparency, accountability, contestability, and ongoing audit.

punchline.text: If nobody's responsible for the algorithm's decisions, then everyone is.

quiz.question: What is the 'responsibility gap' in AI ethics?
options: When algorithmic decisions cause harm but no single person can be held morally accountable

details.summary: AI ethics examines who bears moral responsibility when autonomous systems make decisions that affect human lives. As algorithms drive hiring, sentencing, and medical diagnoses, accountability gaps widen dangerously.
details.whyItMatters: AI systems increasingly make consequential decisions, and unclear responsibility chains mean victims of harmful decisions may have no recourse.
takeaways: Algorithms can embed and amplify human biases
Responsibility gaps arise when no person controls a decision
Transparency and explainability are ethical requirements for AI

faq.question: Who is responsible when an AI system causes harm?
faq.answer: Responsibility may fall on developers, deployers, regulators, or users, but current frameworks often leave gaps where no party is clearly accountable.

faq.question: Why is algorithmic transparency an ethical concern?
faq.answer: If people cannot understand why an algorithm denied them a loan or a job, they cannot challenge the decision, violating basic principles of fairness and accountability.
